LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: WRITING STYLES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.2: Guided Writing: Writing Styles
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing: Writing Styles, part of Writing in Grade 6 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How can you develop a good handwriting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify the family members in a typical nuclear family,

2. place the correct signs (harakat) in given words related to family members,

3. copy sentences about family members from a given display neatly and legibly,

4. work jointly with peers to play scrabble games forming simple Arabic words related to family members,

5. model the Arabic signs from locally available materials and present in class,

6. write a short paragraph about members of the family using appropriate signs (harakat) in neat and legible handwriting,

7. display the neatly written paragraphs in class for review.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify the family members in a typical nuclear family,
2. place the correct signs (harakat) in given words related to family members,
3. copy sentences about family members from a given display neatly and legibly,
4. work jointly with peers to play scrabble games forming simple Arabic words related to family members,
5. model the Arabic signs from locally available materials and present in class,
6. write a short paragraph about members of the family using appropriate signs (harakat) in neat and legible handwriting,
7. display the neatly written paragraphs in class for review.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing: Writing Styles together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and problem solving: This is promoted as the learner follows simple instructions when placing the correct

signs (harakat) in given words related to family members.

Values:
Responsibility: This is promoted as the learner engages diligently in assigned roles when modelling the Arabic signs from

locally available materials and present in class.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Human rights and responsibilities: This is promoted as the learner engages with information on the family which is tied to the

right to association and belonging.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept on family and build on it based on similar concepts in Social Studies.
